column1: # ClawFactory released-artifact ledger.
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS
# The version number stopped identifying the payload. 1.2.0 named THREE distinct
# ClawFactory installers, and before that the Studio filename sat at 1.1.0 across
# two rebuilds because electron-builder interpolates ${version} from
# desktop/package.json and nobody moved it. Each time the digest was the real
# authority and the version was decoration.
# Bumping a number fixes one instance. This file makes the recurrence STRUCTURAL:
# scripts/build_release.ps1 refuses to sign a build whose version already appears
# here against a DIFFERENT digest, and appends a row on every build that signs.
# Reusing a version for new content stops being possible rather than being
# something a tired person has to remember at 2am.
# WHAT THE DIGEST IS, AND WHY THE KIND COLUMN EXISTS
# The gate compares the UNSIGNED compiled bytes. Signing embeds a countersigned
# timestamp, so a signed file's digest differs on every run over identical input
# and could never be compared against anything. The unsigned digest is the one an
# Inno compile makes deterministic.
# Rows written by the gate are kind=unsigned. Rows BACKFILLED from close-outs
# carry kind=signed, because a signed digest is the only value those close-outs
# recorded and the unsigned bytes no longer exist to re-derive. A backfilled row
# is an audit record, NOT a comparison baseline: the gate refuses to compare
# against kind=signed and says so, rather than reporting a mismatch that is really
# just two different things being measured. Only rows the gate wrote are evidence
# the gate saw them.
# Columns, tab-separated:
#   version  artifact  digest_kind  sha256  bytes  date_utc  note
